questions.q: What does the Marketing Manager actually want to see in this project?
options: The sales mix between Individual customers and Store/Reseller customers
A custom marketing RFM segmentation score
A list of every customer's email address
A forecast of next year's sales
questions.explain: The ask is grounded in a real schema distinction already in AdventureWorks2012's Sales.Customer table, not an invented marketing segment.

questions.q: What does the Sales Director want to see?
options: A territory benchmark showing how each territory compares to the company total
A list of individual salesperson commissions
A customer satisfaction score
A product inventory count
questions.explain: The Sales Director's ask is a territory-vs-company-total benchmark view.

questions.q: Why don't the two independently-pulled extracts combine cleanly?
options: Two people pulled overlapping data independently without a shared plan, so duplicate rows and inconsistent values surfaced once combined
AdventureWorks2012 is corrupted
T-SQL cannot join two tables
Power BI refuses to accept two data sources
questions.explain: The messiness comes from combining two separately-pulled extracts, a realistic data-engineering scenario, not from corrupted source data.

questions.q: What three stages make up the pipeline this project builds?
options: T-SQL extract, Python cleaning/joining, Power BI modeling and reporting
Excel, email, PowerPoint
Power Query only, with no SQL or Python
A single manual copy-paste step
questions.explain: The project combines a SQL extraction stage, a Python cleanup/join stage, and a Power BI modeling/reporting stage.

questions.q: In Sales.Customer, what distinguishes an Individual customer from a Store/Reseller customer?
options: Individual customers have PersonID populated; Store/Reseller customers have StoreID populated
Individual customers have a lower CustomerID number
There is no real distinction in the schema
Store/Reseller customers always have a NULL TerritoryID
questions.explain: A Sales.Customer row has either PersonID or StoreID populated, never both — that's the real, schema-grounded segment.
